key_insight: Large-penalty quantum annealing can approach the same biased ground-state sampling as constrained quantum annealing because virtual spin flips generate an effective spin-exchange interaction.
engineering_relevance: This correspondence helps explain sampling bias across penalty-based and constraint-preserving implementations, but does not imply uniform sampling.
method: Compare transverse-field penalty annealing with fully connected XY constrained annealing.
Simulate random graph bipartitioning instances in a closed system.
Use degenerate perturbation theory to relate effective ground-state couplings.
evidence_signal: For the studied instances, Jensen–Shannon divergence between conditional ground-state distributions decreases approximately as the inverse square of the penalty-to-objective energy ratio at sufficiently long annealing times.
watch_item: The correspondence requires suitable perturbative conditions and long annealing times; closed-system results do not establish behavior on noisy hardware.
paper_title: Ground-State Sampling Correspondence between Penalty-Based and Constrained Quantum Annealing
